newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rabbi says Netnayahu promised never to cede land.
newsitem.headline: Rabbi says Netnayahu promised never to cede land.

text.p: An Israeli rabbi accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday of breaking an election promise he gave in writing to the ultra-orthodox Habad movement last May never to cede land to the Arabs.
Habad Rabbi Shmuel Hefer said Netanyahu and cabinet minister Ariel Sharon drafted and signed the letter in exchange for the movement's backing in national elections.
He said the letter included a promise "that no Palestinian state will be established and no other parts of the Land of Israel will be handed over for foreign rule".
AN Israeli official confirmed Netanyahu wrote the letter but denied it was binding or constituted a political agreement.
"The statements by a candidate for prime minister regarding intended policies, should not be viewed as a political agreement of any kind," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said.
Days before the election Habad mounted a huge billboard campaign to help the right-wing candidate get elected under the slogan "Netanyahu is good for the Jews".
Hefer said Netanyahu's readiness now to withdraw Israeli troops from parts of Hebron in the West Bank is a "severe violation" of that commitment.
"Either he did not intend to keep his promise in the first place and that's very severe, or he is unable (to keep his promise) and that is no less severe," Hefer told Israel's Channel Two news.

A successful Israeli-Palestinian summit on Tuesday raised prospects of an agreement on the redeployment in Hebron, the last West Bank town slated for Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 Israel-PLO peace deal.
Netanyahu opposed the 1995 accord and previous Israel-PLO peace deals which launched Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza but has vowed to honour the agreements.
Habad views the West Bank and Gaza, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, as land God promised the Jews which should never be ceded.
